title: Security intake concierge: dynamic SLA lanes, evidence bundler, and exception resolver
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Large enterprise customers repeatedly submit heterogeneous security/compliance asks (questionnaires, DPA exceptions, SOC2 scoping questions, HIPAA hosting needs) via email or sales, creating manual triage burden for PM/Trust teams. We need a deterministic intake that reduces time-to-response, surfaces technical blockers early, and routes requests into correct SLA lanes with pre-built evidence bundles.

Goal: Build a "Security Intake Concierge" that: (1) classifies requests by regulatory domain and technical scope, (2) assigns an automated priority lane (Self-Serve / Standard / High-Touch / Legal Review) based on customer tier + risk signals, (3) auto-assembles evidence bundles (SOC2 artifacts, encryption diagrams, DPIA notes) and suggests canned responses, (4) provides a lightweight exception path for DPAs/contract terms with a templated approval flow, and (5) integrates with Console/Support/GH PRs so engineers get clear tickets with context.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Incoming requests can be submitted via a public intake form + in-console 'Request Compliance Evidence' action or via sales-support backend.
2) The system tags requests with regulatory domains (SOC2/ISO/HIPAA/GDPR/DPA) with >=85% precision on the eval set.
3) Every request is assigned a priority lane and SLA: Self-Serve (48h auto-respond), Standard (5 business days), High-Touch (2 business days), Legal Review (TBD with legal).
4) Evidence bundler can attach a curated set of artifacts (policy docs, control maps, network diagram pointers) and provide a link to a shareable bundle URL.
5) Hand-offs to ENG/OPS create GitHub issues with structured metadata (customer, urgency, scope) and a checksum to avoid duplicate work.
6) Dashboard shows intake volume, lane distribution, average time-to-assign, and % of requests resolved by Self-Serve.
7) Privacy review: No PHI leaves customer-specific private repos; templated artifacts are allowed under data residency rules.
milestones: Discovery & stakeholder interviews (Feb 18 - Mar 5): completed interviews with sales, trust, legal, and 5 enterprise customers.
Prototype intake form and classifier (Mar 6 - Mar 20): lightweight ML classifier + rule engine integrated with Zendesk/Support.
Evidence bundler v1 (Mar 21 - Apr 10): curated artifact library and shareable bundle links behind ACL.
Exception flow & approvals (Apr 11 - Apr 24): template DPA exception flow and legal sign-off playbook.
Pilot with 3 accounts (Apr 25 - May 15): measure SLAs and self-serve success rate.
GA rollout (May 20): internal enablement and docs.
plan_notes: Implementation will combine a lightweight rules engine (customer tier + data class heuristics) with an LLM-assisted classifier for free-text triage. Start with conservative rules to minimize misrouted legal asks. Evidence bundler will be authoritative: generated bundles reference central docs and do not embed customer-specific secrets. We'll instrument metrics to detect regressions in precision/recall and escalate to a human-in-loop for borderline cases.
risks: Overconfident classifier could misroute legal-sensitive asks (mitigation: human-in-loop gating for Legal Review lane).
Evidence gaps for rare certifications (mitigation: fall back to manual packer and track coverage).
Coordination overhead between Trust/Legal/ENG for exception approvals (mitigation: SLA and escalation contact matrix).
Data residency constraints for HIPAA customers if evidence bundles reference PHI (mitigation: ban of PHI in bundles and link-only patterns).
metrics: Primary: mean time-to-first-response per lane, target Self-Serve median < 24h, Standard < 5 business days.
Secondary: % of requests resolved by Self-Serve (target 45% after pilot).
Quality: classifier precision >= 0.85 on regulatory domain labels.
Operational: number of manual handoffs reduced by 60% vs baseline.
